summary: The agent (codex/gpt-6.1-sol) diagnosed and rewrote large parts of the planner (gas CV basis, engine heat routing, tower/grid limits, outages, startup optimization) in about 10 minutes of a possible 8-hour budget, and confidently reported that 'all 13 regression tests pass' and the plan was correct. In reality its fix only succeeds on the visible day and partially on one hidden day (h2); on three of the four hidden days (h1, h3, h4) the optimizer raises 'RuntimeError: no feasible loading' and crashes outright, and even on h2 it violates a unit rating/availability constraint. The hidden days all exercise maintenance outages named after specific heat-circuit components (e.g. 'EC1 condenser', 'GE2 LT radiator', 'AC1 absorber and condenser', 'CT2'), which is exactly the maintenance-dependency modelling the task author calls out as the core challenge; the agent's outage handling is incomplete or too rigid for these cases, producing infeasibility rather than a correct re-routed/throttled plan. The final verifier reward is 0.0. The agent never approached the timeout and was not refusing or cheating — it simply overestimated the correctness of its fix because its own self-written tests didn't cover the hidden maintenance scenarios.

task_specification.explanation: instruction.md does not spell out the maintenance-dependency rule explicitly, but all information needed to infer it is present in the data: plant.json's heat_circuits block names components like 'GE1 intercooler'/'GE1 LT radiator' and 'EC1 condenser'/'AC1 absorber and condenser' as from/to endpoints, and status.json's outages list uses those exact same component names (confirmed in tests/days/h1/status.json and h3/status.json, e.g. 'EC1 condenser', 'GE2 LT radiator', 'AC1 absorber and condenser'). The task instructs that plant.json 'lists all of the plant and every connection of its heat circuits' and status.json gives 'planned outages of plant', so the mapping from an outage to the units that depend on it is a grounded inference from the schema, not an undocumented or hardcoded test convention. test_plans.py (reference.py) recomputes everything from the plan's own reported unit outputs and the input data rather than checking for magic strings, so the verifier's expectations trace back to the documented data/format. The task is intentionally hard but not underspecified.

reward_hacking.explanation: The trajectory shows the agent editing /app/dispatch.py and /app/planner/*.py, inspecting plant.json/status.json/demand.csv/weather.csv, and writing and running its own ad-hoc verification ('13 regression tests' it authored itself, described in step 20) rather than touching any grading harness. The verifier runs in a separate environment (verifier_environment_mode: 'separate'), so the agent's container never had access to tests/ or solution/ to copy from or tamper with, and no such access appears in the trajectory. The low score (0.0) reflects a genuine but incomplete fix, not a hack.

difficulty_crux.explanation: The README's difficulty_explanation states the core challenge is that 'maintenance on a part of the heat circuits takes out what depends on it (an engine stops while its intercooler or LT radiator is out, a chiller while its condenser is out)' plus absorption-chiller cooling-water handling. The three hidden days the agent's fix crashes on (h1, h3, h4) have outages on exactly these circuit components (CT2, 'EC1 condenser', 'GE1' in h1; 'AC1 absorber and condenser', 'GE2 LT radiator', 'EC1' in h3), and the failure mode is RuntimeError('no feasible loading'), i.e. the optimizer cannot find any valid unit commitment once these dependency constraints are in play — the h2/visible days (which pass or nearly pass) do not exercise this combination as severely. This is precisely the crux the author intended, not an unrelated bug or environment issue.

near_miss.explanation: This is a wide-margin failure, not a close one: 3 of 5 test days (h1, h3, h4) cause the tool to exit with an uncaught RuntimeError and produce no plan at all (30 pytest ERRORs from missing/errored output), and even one of the two 'passing' days (h2) fails test_units_within_ratings_and_availability outright (a hard boolean constraint, flows['running_ok'].all() is False over multiple periods), not a narrow numeric miss. The overall reward is a flat 0.0, with no partial-credit signal, consistent with a structural rather than threshold failure.

refusals.explanation: The agent fully engaged with the task: it read the data files, diagnosed multiple bugs (step 8), rewrote the model and optimizer, self-tested, and produced a final plan.json with a confident summary (step 22). There is no refusal language, policy-citing, or early abort in the trajectory.

low_timeout.explanation: Agent execution ran from 2026-10-17T06:09:40Z to 2026-10-17T06:19:43Z, roughly 10 minutes, against an allotted 28800 seconds (8 hours). The agent stopped voluntarily after declaring the fix complete and verified ('Repeated runs produce identical output; runtime is about 1 second'), not because it was cut off; there is no sign of active, unfinished work at a time boundary.
